title: [SEC6] Good: textContent vs innerHTML for XSS prevention
description: Throughout app.js, the code consistently uses textContent instead of innerHTML when rendering user-supplied data: - renderContactList() line 168: 'nameSpan.textContent = getContactName(contact)' - renderChatList() line 267: 'nameSpan.textContent = getChatDisplayName(chat)' - createMessageBubble() line 364: 'body.textContent = msg.body' with CRITICAL comment - createMessageBubble() line 369: 'meta.textContent = getSenderLabel(msg) + ... ts' This prevents XSS injection. A malicious peer could craft a displayName like '' or message body with script tags. innerHTML would execute; textContent treats it as plain text. The code even includes explicit security comments marking where this matters (lines 153-154, 352-353). The pattern is consistent and never breaks it.
